title: Priv: duplicate SAML session-index suppressed audit events and RBAC application drift — urgent patch
creator: Maya Chen
description: A high-severity customer escalation: Private cluster reporting missing audit events and RBAC state drift after IdP failover. Initial triage indicates SAML assertions from the IdP occasionally contain identical session-index values for different authentication flows. Our assertion deduplication path suppresses processing of repeated session-indexes within the dedupe window; that logic inadvertently skipped emitting audit events and did not trigger RBAC refresh for the second assertion, leaving service accounts with stale or incorrect permissions. This ticket implements an urgent patch that preserves audit emission and ensures RBAC reconciliation even when session-index duplication occurs.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure a Private cluster identity provider (SAML) with short session lifetimes and a proxy IdP that can replay assertions.
2) Trigger an IdP failover that causes two near-simultaneous SAML responses using the same session-index but different Subject/attributes.
3) Observe control-plane logs: our SAML dedupe path treats the second assertion as duplicate and returns 200 without processing RBAC mapping or writing audit events.
4) Confirm RBAC assignment reconciliation does not run for the second assertion and audit entries are missing for that authentication event.
5) Reproduce via automated harness that simulates assertion replay and validates audit and RBAC side-effects.
investigation_summary: 03/12 09:12 - Support: customer reported missing audit rows correlated with a tenant IdP failover. 03/12 11:04 - Eng triage: found assertion processor short-circuits on identical session-index tokens inside a 60s dedupe window. 03/12 13:30 - Replay tests: duplication suppressed RBAC binding refresh and audit write; KMS envelope validation still succeeded so we treated assertion as legitimate but skipped downstream side-effects. Logs: control-plane shows 'assertion:dropped:duplicate-session-index' with no audit write calls invoked.
technical_decision: Minimal safe change: alter assertion deduplication to maintain a lightweight assertion fingerprint (hash of session-index + assertion-id + subject) and only suppress complete reprocessing if the fingerprint matches exactly. Always emit a compact audit event (assertion.received duplicate=true) for duplicate session-indexes. Trigger the RBAC reconciliation path whenever attribute mapping differs from current bindings (compare attribute fingerprint). Also add a KMS metadata checksum verification step to detect envelope-transformation races that can cause false duplicates. This reduces the blast radius compared to disabling dedupe entirely. Changes scoped to private control-plane processing and guarded by feature flag 'assertion-dedupe-strict' for canary rollout.
rollout_plan: 1) Implement code change behind feature flag and unit tests (ENG branch).
2) Deploy canary to single private control-plane node for 24h with traffic from low-risk customers (canary group).
3) Enable expanded canary for affected customer environment and run replay harness to simulate failovers.
4) Monitor audit-event rate and RBAC reconciliation metrics for 72h; if stable, promote flag to all private clusters.
5) Post-deploy: run cluster-wide RBAC reconciliation job for windows covering last 48h to repair any drift.
6) Communicate fix and verification steps to impacted customers and SOC.
monitoring_and_alerting: New metric: assertion.duplicates.received (counts duplicates by tenant), alert if >10/min for a tenant
New metric: audit.emit.failures (should be 0), alert on >0
New metric: rbac.reconcile.triggered_from_assertion (counts reconciliations spawned by assertion path)
Dashboard: Private -> Security -> Assertion dedupe (includes duplicate rate, audit events emitted, reconciliation runs)
Pager: P0 if audit.emit.failures > 0 for >5 minutes for any production tenant
